findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - production unwrap() on fallible I/O
findings.failure_mode: Any I/O error (file not found, permissions, disk full) panics the thread instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and propagate with ? or map_err; do not unwrap in production code

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - production unwrap() on fallible parse
findings.failure_mode: A non-numeric second field panics the thread; invalid input aborts the entire batch load
findings.fix: Return Result<Record, ParseError>, use .map_err on parse failure, and propagate errors from the iterator

findings.problem: lossy `as u16` cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: Values above 65535 silently truncate to 16 bits with no error; violates checked-conversion rule
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from() and return a conversion error on overflow, or parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: parts[1] - unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use .get(1) with proper error handling, or use split_once(',', &line) to safely extract the value field

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: A line with zero commas panics via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use .get(0) or split_once to safely access the first field

findings.problem: Hidden I/O (fs::read_to_string + println!) in a function that should be the pure calculation layer
findings.failure_mode: The function leaks side effects into the core, making it untestable without real files and stdout, and conflating data loading with data parsing
findings.fix: Split into two functions: load_raw(path: &str) -> Result<String, IoError> (shell) and parse_records(text: &str) -> Vec<Result<Record, ParseError>> (core). Remove println! from the core path.

findings.problem: println!() is a side effect in a data-parsing pipeline
findings.failure_mode: Logging in the core makes output non-deterministic across runs, pollutes stdout, and couples parsing to console I/O
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely from the core. If instrumentation is needed, return a side-channel type or let the shell layer handle all logging.

findings.problem: Uses split(',') + collect() into Vec<String> instead of split_once for a known two-field format
findings.failure_mode: Allocates a full Vec of all parts and clones each string when only two fields are needed; unnecessary allocation and allocation on every line
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to extract the name and value parts in one pass, then trim and parse each separately

findings.problem: Record struct has pub fields with no invariants; name is an unvalidated String and value is a u16 with no range constraint
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct Record with empty names or out-of-range values; the type does not enforce domain rules
findings.fix: Make fields private, add a fn new(name: String, value: u16) -> Option<Record> constructor that validates invariants (e.g., name non-empty), and expose only getters

findings.problem: Vec grows unbounded with no try_reserve or bounded capacity for known/bounded input
findings.failure_mode: Malformed or extremely large input can exhaust memory without early back-pressure; allocation failure is silently handled by Vec's reallocation strategy
findings.fix: Pre-allocate with try_reserve on the record count (parse line count first) or use try_from for capacity bounds, and handle AllocationError

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions performance
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in the parsing path
no allocation audit showing try_reserve usage for bounded capacity
no benchmark showing second-ring evidence for vectorization or bounds-check removal
no command-evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test execution
residual_risk: This is a static review only with no commands run. Every finding is a BLOCKER: the function uses unwrap on I/O and parse, a lossy as cast, unchecked indexing into split results, hidden println! I/O in the core pipeline, split + collect instead of split_once, unvalidated pub struct fields, and unbounded Vec growth. The crate will not compile under any Holzman-compliant CI gate due to these violations. Zero-cost abstraction claims are unsupported with no benchmarks. Full repair requires refactoring into a functional-core/imperative-shell split with Result-based error propagation, checked arithmetic, split_once parsing, try_reserve, and opaque Record type.
